comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1 and C7 regarding device development and stiffness gradient characterization. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED with no concerns raised about the technical approach or measurements.

Strong agreement on T cell durotaxis demonstration (C2, C8-C12). OpenEval focuses on these specific claims with quantitative evidence, while peer review groups these with additional claims (C13-C17) covering persistence and amoeboid migration. Both find evidence convincing and well-controlled.

OpenEval evaluates persistence and direction-changing behavior (C13-C15) separately as SUPPORTED. Peer review includes these claims in their broader evaluation of durotaxis (R2), accepting that durotaxis occurs without requiring increased persistence.

OpenEval evaluates amoeboid migration mode claims (C16-C17) separately as SUPPORTED. Peer review includes these in their comprehensive evaluation of durotaxis findings, explicitly noting this is the first report of FA-independent durotaxis in amoeboid cells.

Both agree on actin flow mechanosensitivity (C18-C20) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval evaluates these claims separately, while peer review groups them with claims about actin flow not being required for durotaxis (C21-C24).

Both find claims C21-C24 SUPPORTED regarding actin flow not being crucial for durotaxis. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of CK-666 experiments, while peer review accepts these as part of well-designed control experiments in the mechanistic characterization.

Perfect agreement on claims C25-C26 regarding microtubule and intermediate filament independence. Both evaluations find these SUPPORTED as part of the mechanistic dissection showing differential requirements between mesenchymal and amoeboid durotaxis.

Both strongly support NMII requirement for durotaxis (C27-C29). OpenEval evaluates these separately, while peer review groups them with NMIIA-specific claims (C30-C36) in a comprehensive evaluation of the myosin-based mechanism.

Both support NMIIA-specific requirement (C30-C32). OpenEval emphasizes the knockdown data and compensatory changes, while peer review includes these in their broader acceptance of the NMIIA polarization mechanism.

Both support NMIIA polarization findings (C33-C36). OpenEval highlights immunofluorescence quantification and dynamic re-polarization, while peer review accepts this as the central mechanism where NMIIA polarizes toward the soft-matrix-side.

Perfect agreement on evolutionary conservation in Dictyostelium (C37-C41). Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED, with peer review noting this strengthens the conclusion about amoeboid durotaxis being a fundamental mechanism.

Both support the computational model (C6, C47-C48). OpenEval emphasizes model validation through reproduction of experimental observations, while peer review groups these with experimental validation claims (C42-C44) and accepts the model explains durotaxis without strong adhesions.

Both support model predictions and experimental validation (C42-C44). OpenEval evaluates these separately emphasizing agreement between predictions and measurements, while peer review includes them in overall acceptance of the mathematical modeling approach.

Divergence in evaluation type: OpenEval rates claims C69-C71 as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature of C71 regarding contact angle contribution to durotaxis, while peer review finds them SUPPORTED as part of the mechanistic framework without raising concerns about the speculative aspects.
Perfect agreement on formin independence (C78). Both evaluations accept this SUPPORTED negative result as part of defining which cytoskeletal components are not essential for durotaxis.
